events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 11 points
events.body:
→ D1: Conceded as far as the words go: no car trouble, other job or refusal appears, and his only stated ground after the 5-minute mark is the wait (F13, F16). But NS-0 asks whether he cancelled because the rider did not show, and the record shows she was waiting at the pickup point while he had parked 150 m away and refused to approach (F3, F11, F12) — his own words fix the reason for declining the approach, so the charge still fails NS-1(iv). [F3 F11 F12 F13 F16] [NS-0 NS-1]
→ D2: The tap is recorded, but at the moment of the tap the driver was 150 m from the pickup point (F7), and NS-1(i) requires arrival at the pickup point, not merely somewhere inside a 200 m circle; his closest approach in the whole trip was 40 m and he then never closed the gap (F1, F3). [F1 F3 F7] [NS-1]
→ D3 (VOID): The wait is counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival, and the record shows arrival only at 21:26:00 with cancellation 6 min 0 s later (F6, F7); more importantly the wait is irrelevant while the driver sat 150 m away instead of at the pickup point (F3), and DISP-002's 8-minute threshold applied to a driver at the pickup gives the standard he fell short of. [F3 F6 F7] [NS-1 C4]
→ D4: Half-conceded: the three messages and one call are on the record (F5), but the call went unanswered with no recording (F15) and all contact was made from 150 m away after he had decided to wait at the wrong spot (F3, F10), so contact from off the pickup point does not satisfy NS-1(iii) read with NS-1(i). [F3 F5 F10 F15] [NS-1]
→ D5: Presence is not disputed; location is. Being stationary at 150 m from the pickup for 6 min 0 s (F3, F7) is precisely the failure NS-1(iv) and NS-1(i) describe, because the rider cannot board a car that stays a block away (F11, F12). [F3 F7 F11 F12] [NS-1]
→ D6: These facts help the rider, not the driver: he announced Gate B and told her he could not stop at Gate A (F10, F12) while she had already said 'I'm at Gate A, can you come here?'
